Connected by the Outdoors

This month, Patagonia Films introduces Bamb’Amaza: a story of belonging told by a young surfer in South Africa who discovers a different relationship with the sea, and falls in love with it. And inspired by our Surf Movie Nights taking place across Europe, we’re also featuring a look back at two films from our archive: The Physics of Noseriding, and Voices for the Ocean. So sit back, relax, and dive in to a world of wave-riding magic, inspiration, and activism.

Bamb'Amaza

The ocean is an unstoppable force. It’s why so many of us feel drawn to its energy: unyielding, wild, and free. For Othandwayo, living in Cape Town’s Imizamo Yethu, water was always there.

But it’s through surfing that she learned water’s lessons beyond the waves. By embracing the ebb and flow of the ocean, she finds her power, her perseverance, and her people. And even when life gets difficult, she knows that moving with the currents will guide her through almost anything.

Watch

The Physics of
Noseriding

The noseride is one of surfing’s peak moments: part fluid dynamics, part magic. But how does noseriding actually work? What makes this suspension between sea and sky even possible? The Physics of Noseriding explores the question through the eyes of Namaala, a young surfer whose people were flying on the water before the world even knew what surfing was.

Her curiosity invites us to examine the sensation of levitation that unfolds as wave, surfboard and surfer come together for surfing’s fluid dance.

Watch

Voices for the Ocean

We protect what we love. Between the waves they shared on a recent Sumbawa trip, Belinda Baggs, Liz Clark and Moona Whyte also had an opportunity to share how their lives as surfers have led them to a life of committed activism.

We can all speak out for change—and for some of us, the ocean is where we find our voice.
